== Overview ==

'''DataStoreProtocol''' provides a means for clients to upload, download, and interact with S3 objects (though S3 is not required to be used). Objects may be stored either on an external object storage server (such as AWS S3), or directly on the game server if the object data is small enough. The protocol a robust set methods that cover a wide range of UGC needs, including object management/search, a permissions model to set who can access/modify certain objects, notifications for object uploads/updates, user ratings, and optional persistent object storage.

== External File Server ==

Objects may exist either on an external file server, or directly on the game server. Objects which only exist on the game server have [[#DataFlag]] <code>DATA_FLAG_NOT_USE_FILESERVER</code> set on them by the server, and MUST be at most <code>MAX_METABIN_SIZE</code> in size as the object content is stored in the [[#Object MetaBinary]].

Officially, Nintendo uses [https://aws.amazon.com/s3 AWS S3] for their external file server, using [https://aws.amazon.com/cloudfront AWS CloudFront] for delivering uploaded contents to clients. However any server (including non-S3 based servers) can be used, as the game server provides details required to perform an upload (including the upload URL, headers, and root certificate), so long as the server meets the consoles strict requirements. The Wii U and 3DS only support TLS versions 1.0/1.1, and require an RSA certificate, which means the external file server must also support these. Additionally, the Wii U and 3DS will ALWAYS perform uploads via <code>POST</code> requests (using presigned URLs provided by the server, officially) and always with <code>multipart/form-data</code> with the objects contents in the <code>file</code> form field (the client does NOT populate <code>filename</code>, as the "file name" is the S3 key in the bucket, which is provided by the game server).

In the past Nintendo would upload to AWS directly, however they have since [https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/tls-1-2-required-for-aws-endpoints dropped support for TLS versions below 1.2], making direct uploads no longer viable. Either a TLS proxy or an alternative S3 provider is required now (or using some other non-S3-based solution). Most providers, however, only support one or the other of the requirements (either supporting the TLS versions/ciphers but not <code>POST</code>, or supporting <code>POST</code> but not the TLS versions/ciphers), which leaves very few options. To circumvent the TLS deprecation on AWS, Nintendo created a TLS proxy (<code>{bucket_name_here}.p.n.srv.nintendo.net</code>). However this introduces extra processing load compared to uploading directly to the file server, and may not be viable for all developers due to this extra load. The only S3 providers which are known to be compatible are:

* [https://github.com/deuxfleurs-org/garage Garage] - Recommended. Entirely self-hosted and is free/open source. Meets the <code>POST</code> request requirement, but you must bring your own TLS. Currently in use by https://pretendo.network
* [https://github.com/minio/minio MinIO] - Not recommended. Meets the <code>POST</code> request requirement, but has decided to effectively abandon their open source/community version in favor of their paid hosting and AI pivot, and is required to be self-hosted/TLS proxy due to not meeting TLS requirements on their paid hosting
* [https://aws.amazon.com/s3/ AWS] - Not recommended. Meets the <code>POST</code> request requirement, but is very expensive at scale and requires a TLS proxy due to not meeting TLS requirements

Additionally, not many tools/providers support the required TLS/certificate requirements. Many tools, including modern versions of OpenSSL (which is what is shipped by default on most modern systems), have dropped support for TLS 1.0/1.1 entirely, making self-hosted TLS proxies difficult without modifications/building from source or older (and potentially insecure) software versions. Cloudflare is the current easiest/safest way to set up a TLS proxy that works on the Wii U and 3DS (as well as providing overall protection), as Cloudflare Edge Certificates can be [https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/additional-options/minimum-tls configured to support as low as TLS 1.0]. However only [https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/faq/#does-cloudflare-issue-both-rsa-and-ecdsa-certificates-for-universal-certificates Cloudflare Pro and above has access to the RSA certificates] needed. Normally the Pro plan costs [https://www.cloudflare.com/plans/pro $25/m], which would need to be taken into consideration, however open-source projects/teams can apply for a free upgrade to the Pro plan upgrade via the [https://blog.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-new-oss-sponsorships-program/#sponsorship-benefits Cloudflare OSS Sponsorship Program] and is very easy to obtain.

== Object Notifications ==

When an object has [[#DataFlag]] <code>DATA_FLAG_USE_NOTIFICATION_ON_POST</code> and/or <code>DATA_FLAG_USE_NOTIFICATION_ON_UPDATE</code> set, the recipients of the object will get given a "notification" when the object has finished uploading/updating. These are not live notifications like as seen in [[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Protocols/NotificationProtocol|NotificationProtocol]] or [[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Protocols/NintendoNotificationEventProtocol|NintendoNotificationEventProtocol]], nor are they instant messages like as seen in [[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Protocols/MessagingProtocol|MessagingProtocol]] or [[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Protocols/MessageDeliveryProtocol|MessageDeliveryProtocol]]. Instead, these notifications simply point the receiver to the object which created the notification.

A notification for a post is only created once the object actually exists. For objects which use the [[#External File Server]] this is when the upload is completed with [[#CompletePostObjectV1]], [[#CompletePostObject]] or [[#CompletePostObjects]], not when it is prepared, and reporting a failed upload (<code>isSuccess = false</code>) creates no notification. Objects posted with [[#PostMetaBinary]] create theirs straight away, unless <code>DATA_FLAG_NEED_COMPLETION</code> is set, in which case it is created when they are completed. Objects which need review still create notifications, despite still being pending.

A notification for an update is created when the update is completed with [[#CompleteUpdateObject]], not when it is prepared with [[#PrepareUpdateObject]], and reporting a failed upload (<code>isSuccess = false</code>) creates no notification. Updates notify the same users as posts do, including a recipient who made the update themselves. Changing an objects metadata with [[#ChangeMeta]] never creates an update notification, even with <code>MODIFICATION_FLAG_UPDATED_TIME</code> set.

Who is notified depends on the objects access permission, but not its delete permission:

{| class="wikitable"
|-
! Permission !! Notified users
|-
| <code>PERMISSION_PUBLIC</code> || Nobody
|-
| <code>PERMISSION_FRIEND</code> || Every friend of the owner
|-
| <code>PERMISSION_SPECIFIED</code> || Every recipient, including the owner if they are listed
|-
| <code>PERMISSION_PRIVATE</code> || Nobody
|-
| <code>PERMISSION_SPECIFIED_FRIEND</code> || Every recipient who is a friend of the owner
|}

Reading notifications with [[#GetNewArrivedNotificationsV1]] / [[#GetNewArrivedNotifications]] does not remove them by itself, the same notifications are returned until the client passes a later <code>lastNotificationId</code> (see [[#DataStoreGetNewArrivedNotificationsParam]]).

Notifications only last as long as the object they are for. Whenever an object is deleted, every notification for it is deleted too. This includes [[#DeleteObject]] and [[#DeleteObjects]], as well as replacing or removing the object in an [[#Object Persistence]] slot with <code>deleteLastObject</code> set, through [[#PostMetaBinary]], [[#PreparePostObject]], [[#PerpetuateObject]] or [[#UnperpetuateObject]]. A delete which is refused, or a transactional [[#DeleteObjects]] which is rolled back, leaves the notifications alone. Changes which only hide the object or take it away from its recipients do not touch the notifications (meaning, an object which has its status changed will not delete notifications for recipients, and a user who received a notification will not have the notification removed if they are removed as an access recipient from the object). This includes rejecting it or giving it any other [[#DataStatus]] with [[#ChangeMeta]], changing its period to 0, and changing its access permission, even to <code>PERMISSION_PRIVATE</code>. Changing the access permission also does not notify any new recipients.

Each notification is given a unique ID called the "notification ID". Each notification is tied to an [[#Object Data ID]]. Only one notification per object per user may exist, with older ones for the same object for the same user being deleted when a new notification for the object is created for that user (for example, if both <code>DATA_FLAG_USE_NOTIFICATION_ON_POST</code> and <code>DATA_FLAG_USE_NOTIFICATION_ON_UPDATE</code> are set and the owner updates the object before the recipient has checked their notifications, they will only see the notification for the update not the creation). This ID is an incrementing value with the first notification having the ID 1. The creation and deletion of notifications will create gaps in the notification IDs returned by the game server, this is normal and expected.

Additionally, each call to [[#GetNotificationUrl]] creates a new notification using <code>INVALID_DATAID</code> for the user. The purpose of this notification is unknown, as it is not possible to download the notification data for these notifications.

In order for a client to check its notifications, it must locate them from the game server. There are 2 ways for a client to do this:

# [[#GetNotificationUrl]]
# [[#GetNewArrivedNotificationsV1]] / [[#GetNewArrivedNotifications]]

After the client has retrieved its notification IDs, it will store the ID of the most recent notification to use in future requests to [[#GetNewArrivedNotificationsV1]] / [[#GetNewArrivedNotifications]]. The client can then use the the [[#Object Data ID]]s to download the object data the notification is for.

== Object Updates ==

Objects can have both their metadata and underying object data updated. Changing an objects metadata, by itself, does not update the objects modified time. An objects modified time is only updated in these instances:

* Whenever the underlying object data is updated
* Whenever the objects metadata is update with <code>MODIFICATION_FLAG_UPDATED_TIME</code> set
* Whenever the object is removed from an [[#Object Persistence]] slot with [[#UnperpetuateObject]] without being deleted

All objects start at version 1. Each call to [[#PrepareUpdateObject]] hands out the next unused version number, and the object only moves to that version once the update is completed with [[#CompleteUpdateObject]]. A version which is handed out is never handed out again, even if its update fails or is never completed, so the versions an object goes through are not always consecutive. Only the latest version of an object is available by normal clients, though the official servers store each version as its own object in S3 (rather than overwriting the existing data), suggesting Nintendo kept older versions.

== Object Data ID ==

Every uploaded object, whether it uses the [[#External File Server]] or not, is assigned a unique ID known as the "DataID". This ID, along with the object version, is what makes up the S3 key for the object in the [[#External File Server]]. The value is an incrementing ID, and deleted/expired objects do not free their IDs for reuse. In older versions of the protocol the DataID was limited to UInt32, but was changed to UInt64 in NEX 3.5. There are 2 ranges a DataID can be in:

{| class="wikitable"
! Range !! Description
|-
| 900,000-999,999 || Objects in this range are always owned by the server, and cannot be deleted/updated by any normal clients regardless of what the objects permission settings are, nor do they ever expire. Normal users are unable to upload objects in this range, as user uploads always fall into the 2nd range. The methods [[#PostMetaBinaryWithDataId]] and [[#PostMetaBinariesWithDataId]] seem to be only available to server operators, to upload objects in this range
|-
| 1,000,000+ || Regular use. All user uploads always start at 1,000,000 and increment up
|}

=== Data Code ===

Some games allow users to enter a special string to access objects, such as course IDs in Super Mario Maker and Dream Addresses in Animal Crossing: New Leaf. These are called "data codes", and are string representations of the DataID. How a game formats the data code is game-specific, but usually the DataID is transformed from a number into a string (such as converting to hex) and then a checksum is created and inserted somewhere in the data code. The game can then display the data code to users, who can share it with others to input into their own games. When a data code is used, the game first verifies the checksum before trying to perform any NEX methods using the resulting DataID. The server typically does not need knowledge of how these codes are created, as the game client handles the formatting.

== Object MetaBinary ==

Every object may optionally have an associated blob of data, known as the "MetaBinary", stored on the game server. This blob can be up to <code>MAX_METABIN_SIZE</code> in size. The contents of this blob are arbitrary and the meanings are context-specific, as they change between games, between different [[#Object Data Type]]s, etc. Objects which do not use the [[#External File Server]] will have their contents stored in this blob instead, meaning they cannot have an additional associated blob of data.

== Object Data Type ==

Every object is assigned a "data type". Think of this as a categorization system, where a data type represents a category/group that an object belongs to. The list of valid values are arbitrary and the meanings are context-specific, as they change between games. For example, a game may upload user profile information under data type 0, but put each users uploads under data type 100. In another game, data type 100 may be used for user profiles.

== Object Persistence ==

By default all objects, whether it uses the [[#External File Server]] or not, will expire. See [[#Validity Period]] for details. However a user can choose to mark an object they own (and ONLY objects they own) as "persistent". A persistent object will not expire so long as it remains in a slot. Each user has <code>NUM_PERSISTENCE_SLOT</code> number of persistent object slots to store an object in. Each slot may only contain one object. When a user tries to persist an object into a slot that already contains an object, they can choose to delete the existing object or not. If yes, the existing object is immediately deleted. If no, the existing object has its [[#Validity Period]] timer started again, starting from the moment it was removed from the slot. If <code>INVALID_PERSISTENCE_SLOT_ID</code> is used as the slot ID, object persistence is not being used.

== Object Ratings ==

Every object, whether it uses the [[#External File Server]] or not, can be "rated". Each object has <code>NUM_RATING_SLOT</code> number of "rating slots" (IDs 0-15), which are each configured independently and track their own separate rating values/counts. The meaning behind these ratings is game/context-specific. For details on these configurations, see [[#DataStoreRatingInitParam]].

Each user rating for an object slot is tracked as a separate entry, rather than accumulating on a single value. If <code>RATING_FLAG_MODIFIABLE</code> is used, then each user can only have a single rating entry for each of an objects slots, and subsequent ratings simply update that existing entry. Otherwise subsequent ratings create additional entries. The rating slots count is the total number of rating entries for the slot, and the total value is the combined total of all the entries starting from the slots initial value defined in [[#DataStoreRatingInitParam]]. Negative rating values are allowed.

=== Rating Locks ===

Each rating slot may be configured to use a "rating lock". When used, these locks prevent a user from rating that objects slot again for an amount of time. The amount of time is determined by the locks configuration.

When <code>RATING_LOCK_INTERVAL</code> is used, <code>periodDuration</code> is used as the number of seconds (positive) until the lock is lifted.

When <code>RATING_LOCK_PERIOD</code> is used, the lock is set to be lifted at a specific date and time. The date and time is determined based on <code>periodHour</code> and <code>periodDuration</code>. <code>periodHour</code> is the hour of the day the lock will be lifted. The range of hours is between negative and positive 23, with negative values going into the previous day and 0 being midnight. <code>periodDuration</code> determines which specific day the lock is lifted, and must be a valid [[#RatingLockPeriod]]. For example, if a rating slot is configured to use <code>RATING_LOCK_PERIOD_TUE</code> and <code>periodHour</code> is set to 0, and a user rates the slot on March 7th 2024, the lock expiration time is set to 12-3-2024 0:00:00 (the following Tuesday at midnight). Additionally, using <code>RATING_LOCK_PERIOD_DAY1</code> with a negative <code>periodHour</code> will target the last day of the current month.

=== Rating Logs ===

When <code>RATING_FLAG_MODIFIABLE</code> is used, and/or any lock type besides <code>RATING_LOCK_NONE</code> is used, a "rating log" is created when a user rates an objects slot. Trying to query for logs for a slot which do not use these settings will result in <code>DataStore::OperationNotAllowed</code>. The rating log tracks whether or not the caller has rated the slot already, when the lock expires if using a lock, and what the most recent rating value from the caller is.

== Object Referencing ==

Certain operations on an object count as "referencing" said object. The game server keeps track of the number of times an object has been referenced, incrementing the value by 1 each time, and referencing an object can be used to extend its [[#Validity Period]]. These operations include:

* Whenever the object is downloaded via the various "*GetObject*" methods, such as [[#PrepareGetObjectV1]], [[#PrepareGetObject]] and [[#PrepareGetObjectOrMetaBinary]]
* Whenever [[#TouchObject]] is called on the object

This applies no matter who the caller is, including when access is given through the [[#Object Passwords|access password]], when the object is targeted through its [[#Object Persistence]] slot, or when the owner downloads their own object while it is under review. Only a successful call counts as a reference. A call which is refused, such as with <code>DataStore::PermissionDenied</code>, or with <code>DataStore::AlreadyLocked</code> because another lock ID holds the [[#Object Lock ID|read lock]], leaves both the reference count and the referred time alone.

No other method counts as a reference, even if it returns the object. This includes reading the objects metadata ([[#GetMeta]], [[#GetMetas]], [[#GetMetasMultipleParam]], [[#GetSpecificMetaV1]], [[#GetSpecificMeta]]), finding it through [[#SearchObject]], rating it or reading its ratings, changing its metadata, updating its data, persisting it, reading its passwords, and receiving an [[#Object Notifications|object notification]] for it. A new object starts with a reference count of 0, and its referred time is set to the time it was created.

The reference count can also be set directly with [[#ChangeMeta]] using the reference count [[#ModificationFlag]] (<code>0x100</code>). Any value can be set, regardless of how many times the object has actually been referenced, and the count can be both raised and lowered. Later references continue counting from the value that was set, not from what the count was before. For example, if an object has been referenced 3 times and its count is then set to 1, the next reference brings the count to 2.

The reference count is a UInt32. Once it reaches <code>4294967295</code>, further references leave it there rather than wrapping back around to 0.

== Object Passwords ==

When an object is uploaded, the server assigns it a randomly generated set of passwords known as the "access password" and "update password". The object owner can get their objects passwords via [[#GetPasswordInfo]] and [[#GetPasswordInfos]]. The "access password" is used in read-only contexts (viewing metadata, downloading an object, etc.). The "update password" is used in write-contexts (updating metadata, updating the object data, deleting an object, etc.). The "update password" can be changed in the metadata, but the "access password" cannot.

The owner of an object can share these passwords with other users. All permission checks are bypassed if the password matches the given context. Using a password, effectively, treats the request as if it was coming from the object owner.

A password is only checked when it is needed, meaning when the caller would otherwise be denied by the objects permission settings. If the caller already has permission (such as the object owner), the password is ignored entirely, even if it is wrong. If the caller does not have permission and a password is used (meaning, its value is not <code>INVALID_PASSWORD</code>) which does not match the given context, <code>DataStore::InvalidPassword</code> is thrown. If no password is used, <code>DataStore::PermissionDenied</code> is thrown as normal.

== Object Lock ID ==

When <code>DATA_FLAG_USE_READ_LOCK</code> is set, the first time the object is downloaded a "lock ID" can be set by the caller. The server saves this value, and all subsequent downloads MUST use this same lock ID, otherwise <code>DataStore::AlreadyLocked</code>. This seems to have been an older version of the [[#Object Passwords]] system, but lock IDs can be used in conjunction with access passwords (for example, setting a common access password on all a users objects to allow metadata to be seen only by select players through [[#GetMetas]], but setting a unique lock ID on each object to still only allow a specific user to download the object contents).

The lock is cleared only if another call is made to interact with the object using a lock ID of 0. This unlocking call can be made by any user, it does not have to be the current "owner" of the lock.

== Object Tags ==

Every object may have <code>NUM_TAG_SLOT</code> number of tags. Tags are used to add extra metadata about an object that can be used later for searching/filtering purposes. If more than <code>NUM_TAG_SLOT</code> tags are uploaded, <code>DataStore::InvalidArgument</code> is thrown. Each tag can be up to <code>MAX_TAG_LENGTH</code> characters long. If any tag has more than <code>MAX_TAG_LENGTH</code> characters, <code>DataStore::InvalidArgument</code> is thrown. When uploaded, tags are sorted by byte value rather than alphabetically, so digits come before uppercase letters and uppercase letters come before lowercase ones (for example, <code>9nine</code>, <code>banana</code>, <code>1one</code>, <code>Apple</code> are stored as <code>1one</code>, <code>9nine</code>, <code>Apple</code>, <code>banana</code>). They are not trimmed of any leading/trailing white space. If the tag list contains a duplicate string, <code>DataStore::InvalidArgument</code> is thrown.

== Object Strings ==

Object names and [[#Object Tags]] are sent as UTF-8, but the game server processes them as UTF-16. This leads to a few general rules:

* Any character in the Basic Multilingual Plane is accepted and stored unchanged, regardless of script
* Characters outside of the Basic Multilingual Plane (such as emoji, which would need a surrogate pair) cannot be converted. The whole request fails with <code>PythonCore::ConversionError</code> before any DataStore checks are done
* Length limits such as <code>MAX_NAME_LENGTH</code> and <code>MAX_TAG_LENGTH</code> count characters, not bytes. For example, a name may be 64 kanji long, even though each one takes 3 bytes in UTF-8
* Control characters (such as tabs and newlines) are allowed in object names, but any tag containing one is rejected with <code>DataStore::InvalidArgument</code>

== Object Extra Data ==

Starting in NEX 3.5, each object may have a list of associated "extra data". This seems to be internal data, as it is not exposed back to any clients after creation. The official servers seemed to have no limits/checks for this data, allowing for any arbitrary input. This data is likely used for internal tracking systems.

Despite the server allowing any arbitrary input, Animal Crossing: New Leaf (3DS), Xenoblade (Wii U) and Super Mario Maker (3DS and Wii U) all use the same structure for their "extra data" list. Thus, this should (until proven otherwise) be considered the canonical structure of the list:

* Always 6 strings long
* Every string has a max length of 8 characters
* <code>extraData[0]</code> - Platform (<code>CTR</code> for the 3DS (all models), <code>WUP</code> for the Wii U)
* <code>extraData[1]</code> - Region number. <code>CFG_Region</code> on the 3DS, <code>MCPRegion</code> on Wii U
* <code>extraData[2]</code> - Region name. For example, <code>3</code> on 3DS  would use <code>AUS</code> here. An invalid region number will result in <code>Invalid</code> being used here
* <code>extraData[3]</code> - Country number. Comes from <code>SCIGetCafeCountry</code> on the Wii U. See [[Nintendo_Network/Region IDs|Region IDs]]
* <code>extraData[4]</code> - ISO A2 country code. Comes from <code>SCIGetCountryCodeA2(cafe_country)</code> on the Wii U. For example country code 110 (UK) would would be <code>GB</code> here
* <code>extraData[5]</code> - Always empty. Possibly reserved?

For example, this "extra data" sample comes from Animal Crossing: New Leaf:

* <code>extraData[0] = "CTR"</code>
* <code>extraData[1] = "2"</code>
* <code>extraData[2] = "EUR"</code>
* <code>extraData[3] = "110"</code>
* <code>extraData[4] = "GB"</code>
* <code>extraData[5] = ""</code>

== Validity Period ==

Each object is assigned a <code>period</code> value, which is the number of days after upload that the object will remain valid for before becoming expired. An objects validity period must be between 0 and <code>MAX_PERIOD</code>, inclusive. A period of 0 is accepted, but the object is treated as already expired and can never be accessed. This is the case both when an object is uploaded with a period of 0, and when its period is changed to 0 with <code>MODIFICATION_FLAG_PERIOD</code>. See [[#Object Persistence]] for how to prevent an object from expiring. Expired objects are no longer accessible even by the original uploader, and are presumed deleted. An object can have its validity period extended by its <code>period</code> value under the following circumstances:

* Whenever the object is downloaded via the various "*GetObject*" methods and the object has <code>DATA_FLAG_PERIOD_FROM_LAST_REFERRED</code> set
* Whenever [[#TouchObject]] is called on the object and the object has <code>DATA_FLAG_PERIOD_FROM_LAST_REFERRED</code> set
* Whenever the underlying object data is updated
* Whenever the objects metadata is updated with <code>MODIFICATION_FLAG_UPDATED_TIME</code> set. If <code>MODIFICATION_FLAG_PERIOD</code> is used at the same time, use the new period
* Whenever the objects metadata is updated with <code>MODIFICATION_FLAG_PERIOD</code> set. Unlike the others, the new expiry is counted from when the object was last updated, not from the time of the call

For example, if an object is uploaded on January 1st with a <code>period</code> of 90 days (the default), the object will expire on April 1st (or March 31st on a leap year). If on February 15th (45 days after upload) the object has its validity period extended, it will now be set to expire <code>period</code> days after February 15th, which is May 16th (or May 15th on a leap year).

== Common Errors ==

{| class="wikitable"
! Error !! Description
|-
| <code>DataStore::InvalidArgument</code> || The RMC arguments were not valid for the call
|-
| <code>DataStore::NotFound</code> || The object being targeted either does not exist or is not available
|-
| <code>DataStore::OperationNotAllowed</code> || The caller is not allowed to perform the operation, but is not a permissions issue. Such as trying to rate an object the caller owns which has self ratings disabled
|-
| <code>DataStore::PermissionDenied</code> || The caller did not have permission to perform the operation. Such as trying to delete an object the caller does not have permission to manage
|-
| <code>DataStore::UnderReviewing</code> || The object is still under review
|-
| <code>DataStore::InvalidPassword</code> || The password used was either not valid or not for the context it was used in
|-
| <code>DataStore::AlreadyLocked</code> || The object is in read-locked mode and the provided [[#Object Lock ID]] is not valid
|-
| <code>DataStore::OverCapacity</code> || A batch operation had too many inputs
|}

=== PrepareGetObjectV1 ===

=== ChangeMetasV1 ===

Updates multiple objects metadata. Only users with update permissions can perform this operation. See also [[#Object Updates]]. This was replaced by [[#ChangeMetas]] in later versions.

A request must take one of two shapes:

* <code>dataIds</code> is populated and <code>params</code> contains exactly one entry. That entry is applied to every target in <code>dataIds</code>, and the [[#Object Data ID]] defined on the entry is ignored. A target of <code>INVALID_DATAID</code> in <code>dataIds</code> fails with <code>DataStore::NotFound</code>, it does not fall back on the [[#Object Data ID]] defined on the entry
* <code>dataIds</code> is empty and <code>params</code> is populated. Each entry targets the object named by its own [[#Object Data ID]]

Any other combination throws <code>DataStore::InvalidArgument</code> regardless of <code>transactional</code>. This includes <code>dataIds</code> being populated alongside more than one entry in <code>params</code>, <code>dataIds</code> being populated with no entries in <code>params</code>, and both lists being empty. Whichever list holds the targets may contain up to <code>BATCH_PROCESSING_CAPACITY</code> entries. Going over this throws <code>DataStore::OverCapacity</code>, also regardless of <code>transactional</code>.

Targets are updated one at a time, in the order they appear in the request. Duplicate targets are not filtered out or ignored, so an object targeted more than once is updated more than once and keeps the last change made to it. When <code>transactional</code> is true and more than one target fails, the error thrown is the one for the first failing target in the list.

==== Request ====

{| class="wikitable"
! Type !! Name !! Description
|-
| [[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Types#List|List]]&lt;UInt64&gt; || dataIds || Up to <code>BATCH_PROCESSING_CAPACITY</code> update targets
|-
| [[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Types#List|List]]&lt;[[#DataStoreChangeMetaParamV1]]&gt; || params || Up to <code>BATCH_PROCESSING_CAPACITY</code> update details/targets
|-
| Boolean || transactional || If true, all operations must succeed or all changes are rolled back and an RMC error is returned on the first error. If false, errors do not roll back all changes and simply fail for those objects and the results are returned in <code>pResults</code>
|}

==== Response ====

{| class="wikitable"
! Type !! Name !! Description
|-
| [[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Types#List|List]]&lt;[[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Types#Result|Result]]&gt; || pResults || Results of the operations, one per target in the same order as in the request. When <code>dataIds</code> is populated there is one result per entry in <code>dataIds</code>, otherwise there is one result per entry in <code>params</code>. Only populated when <code>transactional</code> is false, otherwise it is assumed every operation succeeded
|}

=== PrepareUpdateObject ===

Requests information needed to update an objects data on the [[#External File Server]]. Only users with update permissions can perform this operation. See [[#Object Passwords]].

Preparing an update only reserves the next version of the object (see [[#Object Updates]]). The objects version, size, modified time and [[#Validity Period]] are left alone until the update is completed with [[#CompleteUpdateObject]]. An update which has not been completed does not stop another one from being prepared, which gets the version after it. Preparing an update does not count as referencing the object (see [[#Object Referencing]]).

* If the object does not exist, has not been completed, or has expired, <code>DataStore::NotFound</code> is thrown
* If the object does not use the [[#External File Server]], <code>DataStore::OperationNotAllowed</code> is thrown
* If the object is under review, only the owner can update it. Anyone else gets <code>DataStore::UnderReviewing</code>
* A rejected object can still be updated by its owner
* The [[#Object Lock ID|read lock]] does not apply, the object can be updated while someone else holds it

==== Request ====

{| class="wikitable"
! Type !! Name !! Description
|-
| [[#DataStorePrepareUpdateParam]] || param || Details on the object the client wants to update and the new size of the object
|}

==== Response ====

{| class="wikitable"
! Type !! Name !! Description
|-
| [[#DataStoreReqUpdateInfo]] || pReqUpdateInfo || Details on how to update the object
|}

=== CompleteUpdateObject ===

Tells the game server the [[#External File Server]] update request has finished. Only the user who prepared the update with [[#PrepareUpdateObject]] can complete it. Anyone else gets <code>DataStore::PermissionDenied</code>, even if they have update permissions.

Completing the update moves the object to the new version and size, and updates its modified time and [[#Validity Period]] (see [[#Object Updates]]). Reporting a failed upload (<code>isSuccess = false</code>) changes nothing, and the same version can still be completed afterwards. A version which was never handed out results in <code>DataStore::NotFound</code>. Completing a version which is already completed, or which is older than the objects current version, is not an error, but changes nothing.

==== Request ====

{| class="wikitable"
! Type !! Name !! Description
|-
| [[#DataStoreCompleteUpdateParam]] || param || Details on the status of the upload
|}

==== Response ====

This method does not return anything.

=== GetNotificationUrl ===

Requests the users [[#Object Notifications]] URL. This differs from [[#GetNewArrivedNotificationsV1]] / [[#GetNewArrivedNotifications]] in that this is a URL that points to an object in the [[#External File Server]], but under a different namespace than UGC objects, and that it will continue to return data even after the notification has been "read". Each user has a unique "notification file" associated with their [[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Types#PID|PID]]. The key for this file is always <code>{number}.{platform}_{game_code}_datastore/ds/1/notify/{pid}</code>, for example <code>10.CTR_JTTA_datastore/ds/1/notify/01880099407</code> is used by Pokemon Bank for the user with [[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Types#PID|PID]] 1880099407, though this is just convention. The game server provides this location, and the game client simply stores it for later use.

Once stored, the game client may not always request a new URL, and will instead reuse the one it already has.

Whenever a user receives a new notification, that notification is stored in the game server and the file this URL points to is updated to contain only the latest notification information. For getting more than just the latest notification, see [[#GetNewArrivedNotificationsV1]] / [[#GetNewArrivedNotifications]]. The file is a plain text file and contains the notification ID, recipient [[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Types#PID|PID]] and game-specific unix timestamp, comma-delimited. The unix timestamp seems to correlate to around when the game was released, and is always the same for all users in the same game (but differs between games). For example, from Swapdoodle:

<pre>
84935077,1870537598,1479103557
</pre>

Additionally, each call to this method creates a notification for the user using [[#Object Data ID]] <code>INVALID_DATAID</code>.

==== Request ====

{| class="wikitable"
! Type !! Name !! Description
|-
| [[#DataStoreGetNotificationUrlParam]] || param || Details on how to request the location of the notification file
|}

==== Response ====

{| class="wikitable"
! Type !! Name !! Description
|-
| [[#DataStoreReqGetNotificationUrlInfo]] || info || Location of the notification file
|}

=== PostMetaBinary ===

Creates an object that is not stored in the [[#External File Server]]. These objects only exist on the game server, their contents are stored in the [[#Object MetaBinary]] and they cannot be retrieved/managed through methods which interact with the [[#External File Server]].

There is no file to upload, so the object is available as soon as it is posted, unless <code>DATA_FLAG_NEED_COMPLETION</code> is used (see [[#DataFlag]]). <code>DATA_FLAG_NOT_USE_FILESERVER</code> is always added to the objects flags. The <code>size</code> field must be 0, even if the [[#Object MetaBinary]] is not empty, otherwise <code>DataStore::InvalidArgument</code> is thrown. The objects size is always stored as 0.

=== PrepareGetObject ===

Requests the information needed to download an object from the [[#External File Server]]. Only users with access permissions can perform this operation. Newer version of [[#PrepareGetObjectV1]].

The object can be targeted either by its [[#Object Data ID]] or by the [[#Object Persistence]] slot it is stored in, using <code>persistenceTarget</code>. If <code>persistenceTarget</code> uses a slot other than <code>INVALID_PERSISTENCE_SLOT_ID</code>, the slot is always used and <code>dataId</code> is ignored entirely, even if the slot turns out to be empty. When targeting a slot:

* An <code>ownerId</code> of 0 is treated as the literal [[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Types#PID|PID]] 0, not as the caller. Since PID 0 has no objects, this always results in <code>DataStore::NotFound</code>. This differs from [[#GetPersistenceInfo]] and [[#GetPersistenceInfos]], which treat an <code>ownerId</code> of 0 as the caller
* If the slot is empty, <code>DataStore::NotFound</code> is thrown. It does not fall back on <code>dataId</code>
* A slot of <code>NUM_PERSISTENCE_SLOT</code> or above is treated as an empty slot and results in <code>DataStore::NotFound</code>, rather than <code>DataStore::InvalidArgument</code> like in [[#GetPersistenceInfo]]

If neither <code>dataId</code> nor <code>persistenceTarget</code> are used, <code>DataStore::NotFound</code> is thrown.

==== Request ====

{| class="wikitable"
! Type !! Name !! Description
|-
| [[#DataStorePrepareGetParam]] || param || Details on the object the client wants to download
|}

==== Response ====

{| class="wikitable"
! Type !! Name !! Description
|-
| [[#DataStoreReqGetInfo]] || pReqGetInfo || Details on how to download the object
|}

=== GetPersistenceInfo ===

Requests information on which object is stored in a specific persistence slot on a specific user. Only users with access permissions can perform this operation. See [[#Object Persistence]].

If the target user has no object in the slot, <code>DataStore::NotFound</code> is thrown. If <code>persistenceSlotId</code> is not a valid slot (<code>NUM_PERSISTENCE_SLOT</code> or above, including <code>INVALID_PERSISTENCE_SLOT_ID</code>), <code>DataStore::InvalidArgument</code> is thrown.

==== Request ====

{| class="wikitable"
! Type !! Name !! Description
|-
| [[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Types#PID|PID]] || ownerId || Target user. If 0, the caller is used
|-
| UInt16 || persistenceSlotId || Target persistence slot. Must be between 0 and <code>NUM_PERSISTENCE_SLOT</code> - 1
|}

==== Response ====

{| class="wikitable"
! Type !! Name !! Description
|-
| [[#DataStorePersistenceInfo]] || pPersistenceInfo || Information about the object stored in the target slot
|}

=== GetPersistenceInfos ===

Requests information on which object is stored in multiple persistence slots on a specific user. Only users with access permissions can perform this operation. See [[#Object Persistence]].

Each slot succeeds or fails on its own. If the target user has no object in a slot, <code>DataStore::NotFound</code> is used as the result for that slot, and its entry in <code>pPersistenceInfo</code> has a <code>dataId</code> of <code>INVALID_DATAID</code>. A slot holding an object the caller does not have access permissions for also only fails its own entry. However if any slot in <code>persistenceSlotIds</code> is not a valid slot (<code>NUM_PERSISTENCE_SLOT</code> or above, including <code>INVALID_PERSISTENCE_SLOT_ID</code>), <code>DataStore::InvalidArgument</code> is thrown for the whole request instead.

If <code>persistenceSlotIds</code> is empty, every slot from 0 to <code>NUM_PERSISTENCE_SLOT</code> - 1 is returned in order, including empty slots. Otherwise the slots are returned in the order they were requested. The same slot can be requested more than once, and is returned once for each time it appears. Because of this, <code>persistenceSlotIds</code> may contain more than <code>NUM_PERSISTENCE_SLOT</code> entries.

==== Request ====

{| class="wikitable"
! Type !! Name !! Description
|-
| [[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Types#PID|PID]] || ownerId || Target user. If 0, the caller is used
|-
| [[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Types#List|List]]&lt;UInt16&gt; || persistenceSlotIds || Target persistence slots. If empty, every slot is targeted
|}

==== Response ====

{| class="wikitable"
! Type !! Name !! Description
|-
| [[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Types#List|List]]&lt;[[#DataStorePersistenceInfo]]&gt; || pPersistenceInfo || Information about the object stored in the target slots. One per target in <code>persistenceSlotIds</code> in the same order as in the request, or one per slot if <code>persistenceSlotIds</code> is empty
|-
| [[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Types#List|List]]&lt;[[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Types#Result|Result]]&gt; || pResults || Results of the operations. One per entry in <code>pPersistenceInfo</code>, in the same order
|}

! Type !! Name !! Description
|-
| UInt16 || persistenceSlotId || Target [[#Object Persistence]] storage slot ID

|-
| Boolean || deleteLastObject || If true, the object already stored in <code>persistenceSlotId</code> (if there is one) is immediately deleted. If false, the object already stored in <code>persistenceSlotId</code> (if there is one) has its [[#Validity Period]] timer started again, starting from the moment it was removed from the slot
|}

==== Response ====

This method does not return anything.

=== UnperpetuateObject ===

Removes an object from the callers [[#Object Persistence]] slots.

If the target slot is already empty, <code>DataStore::NotFound</code> is thrown.

If the object is kept, its modified time is set to the time it was removed from the slot, and its [[#Validity Period]] is counted from then. See [[#Object Updates]].

==== Request ====

{| class="wikitable"
! Type !! Name !! Description
|-
| UInt16 || persistenceSlotId || Target [[#Object Persistence]] storage slot ID to clear
|-

=== ChangeMetas ===

Updates multiple objects metadata. Only users with update permissions can perform this operation. See also [[#Object Updates]]. Newer version of [[#ChangeMetasV1]].

A request must take one of two shapes:

* <code>dataIds</code> is populated and <code>params</code> contains exactly one entry. That entry is applied to every target in <code>dataIds</code>, and the [[#Object Data ID]] defined on the entry is ignored. A target of <code>INVALID_DATAID</code> in <code>dataIds</code> fails with <code>DataStore::NotFound</code>, it does not fall back on the [[#Object Data ID]] defined on the entry
* <code>dataIds</code> is empty and <code>params</code> is populated. Each entry targets the object named by its own [[#Object Data ID]]

Any other combination throws <code>DataStore::InvalidArgument</code> regardless of <code>transactional</code>. This includes <code>dataIds</code> being populated alongside more than one entry in <code>params</code>, <code>dataIds</code> being populated with no entries in <code>params</code>, and both lists being empty. Whichever list holds the targets may contain up to <code>BATCH_PROCESSING_CAPACITY</code> entries. Going over this throws <code>DataStore::OverCapacity</code>, also regardless of <code>transactional</code>.

Targets are updated one at a time, in the order they appear in the request. Duplicate targets are not filtered out or ignored, so an object targeted more than once is updated more than once and keeps the last change made to it. When <code>transactional</code> is true and more than one target fails, the error thrown is the one for the first failing target in the list.

Since [[#DataStoreChangeMetaCompareParam]] compares against the current state of the object, updating the same object more than once in a single request can affect the comparisons made for it. Each comparison sees the changes made by the targets before it, not the object as it was before the request. For example, if the same object is targeted twice with a <code>params</code> entry which changes its name from <code>before</code> to <code>after</code> and compares its name against <code>before</code>, the first update succeeds and the second fails with <code>DataStore::ValueNotEqual</code>, as the name is already <code>after</code> by then.

==== Request ====

{| class="wikitable"
! Type !! Name !! Description
|-
| [[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Types#List|List]]&lt;UInt64&gt; || dataIds || Up to <code>BATCH_PROCESSING_CAPACITY</code> update targets
|-
| [[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Types#List|List]]&lt;[[#DataStoreChangeMetaParam]]&gt; || params || Up to <code>BATCH_PROCESSING_CAPACITY</code> update details/targets
|-
| Boolean || transactional || If true, all operations must succeed or all changes are rolled back and an RMC error is returned on the first error. If false, errors do not roll back all changes and simply fail for those objects and the results are returned in <code>pResults</code>
|}

==== Response ====

{| class="wikitable"
! Type !! Name !! Description
|-
| [[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Types#List|List]]&lt;[[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Types#Result|Result]]&gt; || pResults || Results of the operations, one per target in the same order as in the request. When <code>dataIds</code> is populated there is one result per entry in <code>dataIds</code>, otherwise there is one result per entry in <code>params</code>. Only populated when <code>transactional</code> is false, otherwise it is assumed every operation succeeded
|}

Presumably creates an object that does not use the [[#External File Server]] using a set [[#Object Data ID]] instead of letting the server generate one. |}

This method does not return anything.

=== DataStoreChangeMetaParamV1 ===

Holds details for how the game server should update an existing objects metadata. This was replaced by [[#DataStoreChangeMetaParam]] in later versions.

The fields being updated are determined by <code>modifiesFlag</code>. Every field is always sent, but only the fields named in <code>modifiesFlag</code> are applied. If a field is not being updated, its value is in a "zeroed" state. Undefined bits in <code>modifiesFlag</code> are ignored. If <code>modifiesFlag</code> is <code>MODIFICATION_FLAG_NONE</code>, nothing is changed but the request still succeeds.

Unlike [[#DataStoreChangeMetaParam]], this version has no fields for the reference count, data type or status. <code>modifiesFlag</code> can still name them, but they are not all handled the same way:

* The reference count flag (<code>0x100</code>) and <code>MODIFICATION_FLAG_STATUS</code> are accepted, but do nothing
* <code>MODIFICATION_FLAG_DATA_TYPE</code> is refused with <code>DataStore::InvalidArgument</code>

{| class="wikitable"
! Type !! Name !! Description
|-
| UInt64 || dataId || The [[#Object Data ID]] being updated
|-
| [[#ModificationFlag]] || modifiesFlag || Which fields are being updated
|-
| [[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Types#String|String]] || name || New object name
|-
| [[#DataStorePermission]] || permission || New permission level settings for accessing the object
|-
| [[#DataStorePermission]] || delPermission || New permission level settings for updating the object
|-
| UInt16 || period || New [[#Validity Period]]
|-
| [[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Types#qBuffer|qBuffer]] || metaBinary || New [[#Object MetaBinary]]
|-
| [[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Types#List|List]]&lt;[[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Types#String|String]]&gt; || tags || New [[#Object Tags]]
|-
| UInt64 || updatePassword || [[#Object Passwords]]
|}

=== DataStoreChangeMetaParam ===

Holds details for how the game server should update an existing objects metadata. Newer version of [[#DataStoreChangeMetaParamV1]].

The fields being updated are determined by <code>modifiesFlag</code>. Every field is always sent, but only the fields named in <code>modifiesFlag</code> are applied. If a field is not being updated, its value is typically in a "zeroed" state, though the game server ignores it entirely and does not validate it, so even an invalid value is accepted. Undefined bits in <code>modifiesFlag</code> are ignored. If <code>modifiesFlag</code> is <code>MODIFICATION_FLAG_NONE</code>, nothing is changed but the request still succeeds.

<code>compareParam</code> works independently of <code>modifiesFlag</code>. The fields being compared are determined only by <code>compareParam.comparisonFlag</code>, so a comparison is still made when <code>modifiesFlag</code> is <code>MODIFICATION_FLAG_NONE</code> or does not include the field being compared. In other words, <code>modifiesFlag</code> decides which new values are validated and applied, and <code>comparisonFlag</code> decides which current values must match before anything is applied. See [[#DataStoreChangeMetaCompareParam]] for how values are compared.

The checks are made in this order, and the first one to fail is thrown:

# The caller must have update permission for the object, otherwise <code>DataStore::PermissionDenied</code>. See [[#Object Passwords]]
# The new values named in <code>modifiesFlag</code> must be valid, otherwise <code>DataStore::InvalidArgument</code>. This happens even if the comparison would not match
# The fields named in <code>compareParam.comparisonFlag</code> must match the current state of the object, otherwise <code>DataStore::ValueNotEqual</code>

=== DataStoreReqGetNotificationUrlInfo ===

URL data for where the users latest [[#Object Notifications]] notification information is located in the [[#External File Server]]. To construct the final URL, combine <code>url</code>, <code>key</code> and <code>query</code> back-to-back.

{| class="wikitable"
! Type !! Name !! Description
|-
| [[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Types#String|String]] || url || Base URL. For example, <code>https://ctr-jtta-live.p.n.srv.nintendo.net/</code>
|-
| [[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Types#String|String]] || key || The [[#External File Server]] key. This uses a different namespace than regular objects, and is treated as the request path. For example, <code>10.CTR_JTTA_datastore/ds/1/notify/01880099407</code> where <code>01880099407</code> is the decimal PID of the user, padded
|-
| [[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Types#String|String]] || query || Query parameters for the request. For example, <code>?AWSAccessKeyId=AKIAIZIRU4FPYFNKPX3A&Expires=2092069557&Signature=5Y0vXYtxyXQXB%2Fu2Sowv%2Fm1AC8E%3D</code>
|-
| [[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Types#Buffer|Buffer]] || rootCaCert || Root CA for the request. Can be left empty if not used
|}

=== DataStoreGetNewArrivedNotificationsParam ===

Used by [[#GetNewArrivedNotificationsV1]] and [[#GetNewArrivedNotifications]] to request a list of unread [[#Object Notifications]].

{| class="wikitable"
! Type !! Name !! Description
|-
| UInt64 || lastNotificationId || The last notification ID the client got from the server, or 0 if they have never seen any notifications. The game server only returns notifications for the user sent after this ID. The game server considers all notifications for the user prior to this ID as "read" and will no longer return them in future requests, even if future requests use a lower notification ID again
|-
| UInt16 || limit || The maximum number of notifications to return, oldest first. Any value from 1 to 99 is used as is. 0, or any value of 100 or more, returns at most 20. When more notifications remain, <code>pHasNext</code> is set in the response
|}

=== DataStorePermission ===

A single object permission setting. Each object has a permission setting for accessing the object, and a setting for updating the object. Using an [[#Object Passwords]] will bypass these permissions.

{| class="wikitable"
! Type !! Name !! Description
|-
| [[#Permission]] || permission || The permission level
|-
| [[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Types#List|List]]&lt;[[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Types#PID|PID]]&gt; || recipientIds || Specific users who are given permission to perform operations. Only usable when using either <code>PERMISSION_SPECIFIED</code> or <code>PERMISSION_SPECIFIED_FRIEND</code>, otherwise <code>DataStore::InvalidArgument</code> is thrown
|}

=== DataStoreRatingInitParamWithSlot ===

Initializes a specific [[#Object Ratings]] rating slot with the given settings.

Each slot can only be initialized once per object. If a list of these contains more than one entry for the same slot, <code>DataStore::OperationNotAllowed</code> is thrown, rather than the last entry being used.

{| class="wikitable"
! Type !! Name !! Description
|-
| SInt8 || slot || The slot to initialize. Must be between 0 and <code>RATING_SLOT_MAX</code>, otherwise <code>DataStore::InvalidArgument</code> is thrown
|-
| [[#DataStoreRatingInitParam]] || param || Slot settings
|}

=== DataStorePersistenceInitParam ===

Used to insert an object being created into a users [[#Object Persistence]] storage during upload.

{| class="wikitable"
! Type !! Name !! Description
|-
| UInt16 || persistenceSlotId || Target [[#Object Persistence]] storage slot ID
|-
| Boolean || deleteLastObject || If true, the object already stored in <code>persistenceSlotId</code> (if there is one) is immediately deleted. If false, the object already stored in <code>persistenceSlotId</code> (if there is one) has its [[#Validity Period]] timer started again, starting from the moment it was removed from the slot
|}

=== DataStoreChangeMetaCompareParam ===

Data on which existing object metadata is compared to before updating the objects metadata. If any fields on this class do not match the corresponding metadata for the object prior to update, <code>DataStore::ValueNotEqual</code> is thrown.

Only the fields named in <code>comparisonFlag</code> are compared, the rest are ignored regardless of their value. Undefined bits in <code>comparisonFlag</code> are ignored. The comparison is made against the object as it is before the change is applied, so comparing against the value being set in the same request does not match. When comparing:

* [[#Object Tags]] match regardless of their order
* Permissions only match if both the permission level and the recipient list match
* The status is the objects current status, so an object still under review is compared as <code>DATA_STATUS_PENDING</code>

{| class="wikitable"
! Type !! Name !! Description
|-
| [[#ComparisonFlag]] || comparisonFlag || Determines which fields to compare
|-
| [[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Types#String|String]] || name || Name to compare, or empty if not comparing
|-
| [[#DataStorePermission]] || permission || Access permission level settings to compare, or empty if not comparing
|-
| [[#DataStorePermission]] || delPermission || Update permission level settings to compare, or empty if not comparing
|-
| UInt16 || period || Period to compare, or empty if not comparing
|-
| [[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Types#qBuffer|qBuffer]] || metaBinary || [[#Object MetaBinary]] to compare, or empty if not comparing
|-
| [[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Types#List|List]]&lt;[[Nintendo_Network/NEX/Types#String|String]]&gt; || tags || [[#Object Tags]] to compare, or empty if not comparing
|-
| UInt32 || referredCnt || Reference count to compare, or empty if not comparing
|-
| UInt16 || dataType || [[#Object Data Type]] to compare, or empty if not comparing
|-
| [[#DataStatus]] || status || Status to compare, or empty if not comparing
|}

== Enums ==

=== Permission ===

Determines the permission level of an object in [[#DataStorePermission]].

<pre>
enum Permission : uint8_t {
  ...
};
</pre>

{| class="wikitable"
! Name !! Value !! Description
|-
| <code>PERMISSION_PUBLIC</code> || 0 || Anyone can perform the operation
|-
| <code>PERMISSION_FRIEND</code> || 1 || Only the object owner and their friends can perform the operation
|-
| <code>PERMISSION_SPECIFIED</code> || 2 || Only the object owner and the specified users can perform the operation
|-
| <code>PERMISSION_PRIVATE</code> || 3 || Only the object owner can perform the operation
|-
| <code>PERMISSION_SPECIFIED_FRIEND</code> || 4 || Only the object owner and the specified friends can perform the operation. If a friend is specified and then removed as a friend, that user loses permission
|}

=== DataStatus ===

Determines the availability status of an object. All other values throw <code>DataStore::InvalidArgument</code> when they try to be used.

The status can be changed with [[#ChangeMeta]] using <code>MODIFICATION_FLAG_STATUS</code>. This is not limited to the object owner, anyone with update permissions for the object can change its status, including rejecting someone elses object.

<pre>
enum DataStatus : uint8_t {
  ...
};
</pre>

{| class="wikitable"
! Name !! Value !! Description
|-
| <code>DATA_STATUS_NONE</code> || 0 || The object has been successfully uploaded and is available to anyone with access permissions. See [[#DataStorePermission]]
|-
| Unknown || 1 || Purpose unknown. Can be set through [[#ChangeMeta]], after which the object can no longer be found by anyone, including the owner (<code>DataStore::NotFound</code>)
|-
| <code>DATA_STATUS_PENDING</code> || 2 || The object is uploaded but pending review. This state is automatically set when an object is uploaded with <code>DATA_FLAG_NEED_REVIEW</code> set. The object can only be seen by the owner until review is finished. Anyone besides the owner who tries to query for objects under review will result in <code>DataStore::UnderReviewing</code>
|-
| Unknown || 3 || Purpose unknown. Can be set through [[#ChangeMeta]], after which the object can no longer be found by anyone, including the owner (<code>DataStore::NotFound</code>)
|-
| Unknown || 4 || Purpose unknown. Can be set through [[#ChangeMeta]], after which the object can no longer be found by anyone, including the owner (<code>DataStore::NotFound</code>)
|-
| <code>DATA_STATUS_REJECTED</code> || 5 || The object has failed review and has been rejected. The object is not available to anyone, including the owner, and behaves as if the object does not exist (<code>DataStore::NotFound</code>). The only exception to this is if the owner uses [[#SearchObject]] or [[#SearchObjectLight]] with either <code>SEARCH_TYPE_OWN_REJECTED</code> or <code>SEARCH_TYPE_OWN_ALL</code>
|}

| <code>SEARCH_TYPE_SEND_FRIEND</code> || 2 || Objects owned by the current user and which have their access [[#Permission]] set to <code>PERMISSION_FRIEND</code>

|-
| <code>SEARCH_TYPE_SEND</code> || 5 || Objects owned by the current user and which have their access [[#Permission]] set to <code>PERMISSION_FRIEND</code>, <code>PERMISSION_SPECIFIED</code> or <code>PERMISSION_SPECIFIED_FRIEND</code>
|-

|-
| <code>SEARCH_TYPE_RECEIVED</code> || 8 || Objects which have their access [[#Permission]] set to either <code>PERMISSION_SPECIFIED</code> or <code>PERMISSION_SPECIFIED_FRIEND</code> and which have the current user set as a recipient, or objects owned by the friends of the current user which have their access [[#Permission]] set to <code>PERMISSION_FRIEND</code>

|-
| <code>SEARCH_TYPE_OWN_PENDING</code> || 12 || Objects owned by the current user and which have their [[#DataStatus]] set to <code>DATA_STATUS_PENDING</code>
|-
| <code>SEARCH_TYPE_OWN_REJECTED</code> || 13 || Objects owned by the current user and which have their [[#DataStatus]] set to <code>DATA_STATUS_REJECTED</code>
|-
| <code>SEARCH_TYPE_OWN_ALL</code> || 14 || Objects owned by the current user and which have their [[#DataStatus]] set to <code>DATA_STATUS_NONE</code>, <code>DATA_STATUS_PENDING</code> or <code>DATA_STATUS_REJECTED</code>
|}

=== RatingLockType ===

Determines how to lock the current user out of future ratings on the slot.

<pre>
enum RatingLockType : uint8_t {
  ...
};
</pre>

{| class="wikitable"
! Name !! Value !! Description
|-
| <code>RATING_LOCK_NONE</code> || 0 || No locking used. The user is allowed to freely rate the slot as much as they want
|-
| <code>RATING_LOCK_INTERVAL</code> || 1 || The user cannot rate the same slot again for a specified amount of time. See [[#Rating Locks]] for details
|-
| <code>RATING_LOCK_PERIOD</code> || 2 || The user cannot rate the same slot again until a specific date/time. See [[#Rating Locks]] for details
|-
| <code>RATING_LOCK_PERMANENT</code> || 3 || The user can never rate the slot again
|}

== Flags ==

=== DataFlag ===

General object flags. When uploading an object, setting any bit which is not listed here throws <code>DataStore::InvalidArgument</code>, rather than the bit being ignored.

<pre>
enum DataFlag : uint32_t {
  ...
};
</pre>

{| class="wikitable"
! Name !! Value !! Description
|-
| <code>DATA_FLAG_NONE</code> || 0x00 || No flags set
|-
| <code>DATA_FLAG_NEED_REVIEW</code> || 0x01 || The object needs to be reviewed before it becomes available. See [[#DataStatus]]
|-
| <code>DATA_FLAG_PERIOD_FROM_LAST_REFERRED</code> || 0x02 || The object can have its [[#Validity Period]] extended when referenced
|-
| <code>DATA_FLAG_USE_READ_LOCK</code> || 0x04 || Enables object read locking. See [[#Object Lock ID]]
|-
| <code>DATA_FLAG_USE_NOTIFICATION_ON_POST</code> || 0x08 || Creates an [[#Object Notifications|object notification]] for the object recipients when the object has finished uploading. This can also be used with objects that do not use the [[#External File Server]], in which case the notification is created as soon as the object is posted with [[#PostMetaBinary]]
|-
| <code>DATA_FLAG_USE_NOTIFICATION_ON_UPDATE</code> || 0x10 || Creates an [[#Object Notifications|object notification]] for the object recipients when the object has finished updating. This cannot be used with objects that do not use the [[#External File Server]], as they can never be updated. Using it with [[#PostMetaBinary]] results in <code>DataStore::InvalidArgument</code>
|-
| <code>DATA_FLAG_NOT_USE_FILESERVER</code> || 0x20 || The object does not use the [[#External File Server]] and only exists as [[#Object MetaBinary]] on the game server. This flag is automatically assigned to every object posted with [[#PostMetaBinary]] by the server. It can be set by the caller when using [[#PostMetaBinary]], which changes nothing, but setting it when posting an object which does use the [[#External File Server]] (such as with [[#PreparePostObject]]) will result in <code>DataStore::InvalidArgument</code>
|-
| <code>DATA_FLAG_NEED_COMPLETION</code> || 0x40 || Requires an object which does not use the [[#External File Server]] to be "completed" before it becomes available. Objects which use the [[#External File Server]] always need to be completed once their upload has finished, so this flag changes nothing for them. Objects posted with [[#PostMetaBinary]] have nothing to upload, so they are normally available straight away and cannot be completed. With this flag set they behave like objects on the [[#External File Server]] instead, returning <code>DataStore::NotFound</code> when queried for until [[#CompletePostObject]], [[#CompletePostObjectV1]] or [[#CompletePostObjects]] is called on them. Objects which have not been marked as "completed" will be deleted a few hours after upload, and the owner will no longer be able to mark them as "completed"
|}

=== ModificationFlag ===

Used to indicate what properties of an object have been modified.

<pre>
enum ModificationFlag : uint32_t {
  ...
};
</pre>

{| class="wikitable"
! Name !! Value !! Description
|-
| <code>MODIFICATION_FLAG_NONE</code> || 0x000 || No changes
|-
| <code>MODIFICATION_FLAG_NAME</code> || 0x001 || The object name has been updated
|-
| <code>MODIFICATION_FLAG_ACCESS_PERMISSION</code> || 0x002 || The object access permission has been updated
|-
| <code>MODIFICATION_FLAG_UPDATE_PERMISSION</code> || 0x004 || The object update permission (also seen as "delete permission") has been updated
|-
| <code>MODIFICATION_FLAG_PERIOD</code> || 0x008 || The object period has been updated. The object then expires this number of days after it was last updated, rather than after the time of the call
|-
| <code>MODIFICATION_FLAG_METABINARY</code> || 0x010 || The [[#Object MetaBinary]] has been updated
|-
| <code>MODIFICATION_FLAG_TAGS</code> || 0x020 || The [[#Object Tags]] have been updated
|-
| <code>MODIFICATION_FLAG_UPDATED_TIME</code> || 0x040 || Forces the server to update the objects "updated time". This also extends the objects validity period by either the current period, or the new period if <code>MODIFICATION_FLAG_PERIOD</code> is also set
|-
| <code>MODIFICATION_FLAG_DATA_TYPE</code> || 0x080 || The [[#Object Data Type]] has been updated
|-
| Unknown || 0x100 || The object reference count has been updated
|-
| <code>MODIFICATION_FLAG_STATUS</code> || 0x200 || The object [[#DataStatus]] has been updated
|}

=== ComparisonFlag ===

Before the objects data is updated, the current object data is checked against the data in [[#DataStoreChangeMetaCompareParam]]. These flags tell the server which data to compare. If any of the compared fields do not match, the object data is not updated and <code>DataStore::ValueNotEqual</code> is thrown.

<pre>
enum ComparisonFlag : uint32_t {
  ...
};
</pre>

{| class="wikitable"
! Name !! Value !! Description
|-
| <code>COMPARISON_FLAG_NONE</code> || 0x000 || No comparison
|-
| <code>COMPARISON_FLAG_NAME</code> || 0x001 || Compare names
|-
| <code>COMPARISON_FLAG_ACCESS_PERMISSION</code> || 0x002 || Compare access permissions
|-
| <code>COMPARISON_FLAG_UPDATE_PERMISSION</code> || 0x004 || Compare update permissions
|-
| <code>COMPARISON_FLAG_PERIOD</code> || 0x008 || Compare periods
|-
| <code>COMPARISON_FLAG_METABINARY</code> || 0x010 || Compare MetaBinaries
|-
| <code>COMPARISON_FLAG_TAGS</code> || 0x020 || Compare tags
|-
| <code>COMPARISON_FLAG_DATA_TYPE</code> || 0x040 || Compare data types
|-
| Unknown || 0x080 || Compare reference counts
|-
| <code>COMPARISON_FLAG_STATUS</code> || 0x100 || Compare statuses
|-
| <code>COMPARISON_FLAG_ALL</code> || 0xFFFF || Compare everything
|}

  ...

{| class="wikitable"

| <code>RESULT_FLAG_RATINGS</code> || 0x2 || Return [[#Object Ratings]]
|-
| <code>RESULT_FLAG_METABINARY</code> || 0x4 || Return [[#Object MetaBinary]]

=== RatingFlag ===

Determines how to handle how user ratings are applied to objects.

<pre>
enum RatingFlag : uint8_t {
  ...
};
</pre>

{| class="wikitable"
! Name !! Value !! Description
|-
| <code>RATING_FLAG_MODIFIABLE</code> || 0x04 || When set, each user can only have one rating per slot. If the user has already rated the slot, update the existing rating rather than creating another rating entry
|-
| <code>RATING_FLAG_ROUND_MINUS</code> || 0x08 || When set, ratings less than 0 are rounded to 0
|-
| <code>RATING_FLAG_DISABLE_SELF_RATING</code> || 0x10 || When set, disables the ability for the object owner to rate the object. If the owner tries to rate the object, <code>DataStore::OperationNotAllowed</code> is thrown
|}

=== RatingInternalFlag ===

Determines how a rating slot should handle an incoming rating value.

<pre>
enum RatingInternalFlag : uint8_t {
  ...
};
</pre>

{| class="wikitable"
! Name !! Value !! Description
|-
| <code>RATING_INTERNAL_FLAG_USE_RANGE_MIN</code> || 0x2 || When set, the incoming rating is checked against the minimum configured value. If below the minimum, <code>DataStore::InvalidArgument</code> is thrown. If not set, do not check for a minimum value
|-
| <code>RATING_INTERNAL_FLAG_USE_RANGE_MAX</code> || 0x4 || When set, the incoming rating is checked against the maximum configured value. If above the maximum, <code>DataStore::InvalidArgument</code> is thrown. If not set, do not check for a maximum value
|}
